doc.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

title: Brothers Tom and Robert Boynes
summary: Burns names brother Tom (James) Boynes, a piano player in New Orleans, and dead brother Robert.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. You got a brother too? Is he still living? Yeah, he's living. He's in New Orleans. Oh, in New Orleans. What's his name? He played piano, funky butts. We call him the funky butts. What's his name? James Boynes. We call him Tom. Oh, yeah. Everybody know him in Tomy Boynes.

Yeah, he still plays around, you know. What does he play? He plays something like, you know, what I play. Oh, piano? Yeah. He played a different kind of blues to me, you know. He played kind of funny.
Yeah, he's a couple of years or so. How many years? Two years. Two years older than me.
Do you know where he lives now in New Orleans?
Yeah. Give him Tom's address. He's still living, yeah. He rang me up.
And he knew all these Burrell House guys too?
Well, he know quite a few of them, he do.
You had to ask him why you was there.
Yeah, I didn't know. I never heard about him. I just knew.
Well, it had been so long, darling. You know, he'd die out, you know. Yeah. He'd suck your ass.
He played something for me when I was down there. I'd say, Tom, you got them same old blues there. Yeah? Yeah. He played some funny kind of blues. Something on the order of Buster Anderson.
Something like it, yeah. Not even right there. Other brother, Babe, the one was dead. Well, he played like me.
Oh, you got another brother. Well, the one was dead.
That's Robert Boynton. Oh, Robert. Yeah, yeah. He's dead, him. The one living, Tom. Yeah. He's living. Yeah. He's dead.
